newsitem.title: UK: IPE Oct gas oil ends $1.75 a tonne higher.
newsitem.headline: IPE Oct gas oil ends $1.75 a tonne higher.

text.p: IPE Oct gas oil ended $1.75 higher at $247.25 per tonne after slipping back from the day's high of $250 in a bull market where only the brave would dare go short, brokers said.

Dealers said the prompt gas oil spread held at $6.50 at the close but was likely to come under some pressure as dealers began rolling positions forward into November ahead of October's expiry on Thursday.
"The spread seems to have held. It's good backwardation holding. Maybe it will come in a bit as people roll forward length," a futures broker said.
"At this time of the contract, there's nobody there to support it and no fresh length will come in so it might be pushed down a bit," he added.
Gas oil futures soared to an intra-day high of $250, the highest level for the near-month contract in more than five years, before slipping back to settle at $247.25.
Gas oil has been moving steadily higher on fears of a supply crunch in the Atlantic Basin as the first chill of winter hit the U.S. northeast last week.
The Oct/Nov gas oil spread was at $6.50 at the close. Nov gas oil settled $5.25 up at $240.75.

IPE Brent crude was also riding high on firm gas oil, holding near the $24 level for much of the afternoon session after rising to an intra-day high $24.25 a barrel after NYMEX heating oil came in strong in the early London afternoon.
Nov Brent was trading 26 cents higher at $24.11 a barrel at 1710 GMT. The next target was the post Gulf War high of $24.39.
